text:
samira: @mike customer MantisBay reported intermittent p99 spikes on embeddings.v1/search since ~09:30 UTC. They say it's affecting their realtime search UX, lots of 600-900ms p99s vs usual ~120ms. they posted a couple trace ids: trace_2026_0915_A and trace_2026_0915_B

mike: on it. do we have tenant id / api key? need traces + client payload sizes.

samira: tenant: mantisbay-prod-43, api key masked in thread. examples from customer: small single-embed requests (payload ~1 text field, 80 tokens). latency only spikes on peak minutes (short bursts). they said embedding unit usage didn't change much. attaching their client timeline screenshot link: https://img.redwood.example/mantisbay/spike.png

ryan: curious if this is noisy-neighbor or backend batching configuration. do we see concurrent request storms from that tenant at those times?

ingrid: copying p99 heatmap for the host pool they hit (from console):
```
hostpool: g4dn-x-large-01
p95: 130ms
p99: 720ms (spikes 800-950ms at 09:30)
concurrency: burst to 48 conns at 09:30
avg batch size: 14 -> jumps to 60 during spike
```

mike: aha avg batch size jumps to 60 for tiny requests — that explains slow tails. runtime batching window probably grew due to sudden burst and queueing. we throttle per-tenant but looks like they were routed to shared pool with relaxed reservation.

samira: customer says they didn't increase call volume. they suspect retries from a frontend bug might be causing short retry storms. they can follow up with their frontend team.

ryan: can we verify if the KV cache hit rate changed? if cache cold we'd see more compute cost but not necessarily queueing.

ingrid: KV cache hit rate for tenant: dropped from 98% -> 40% during the spike window. logs show a sequence of near-simultaneous new conversation IDs (client-side rotated session ids). looks like prefix cache warming thrash.

mike: plan: 1) mitigate quickly by placing mantisbay on a soft per-tenant reservation (temp) or put on an allowlist for dedicated burst capacity; 2) long-term suggest client change to avoid hot restart of session ids; 3) tune runtime batching to cap batch size for that tenant while we investigate.

samira: customer asking for ETA. we should offer a quick mitigation and followups.

ryan: I'm going to create a temporary reservation of 4 slots in pool g4dn-x-large-01 for mantisbay-prod-43 for 1 hour to dampen queueing. applying now.

deploy-bot: reservation.create request accepted: id=resv-7991, tenant=mantisbay-prod-43, slots=4, pool=g4dn-x-large-01, expires=1h

mike: also applying a per-tenant batch cap override:
```
PATCH /operator/v1/tenants/mantisbay-prod-43/config
{
  "batching": {"max_batch_size": 20, "burst_protection": true}
}
```

mike: pushed. will monitor p99. meanwhile asking customer for full traces for those trace ids - we need timing and server-side route ids.

samira: customer confirmed they see immediate improvement after 3m. p99 back to ~150-220ms. they are happy with short-term fix. will follow up re frontend retries. :thumbsup:

ryan: we should keep the reservation for another hour to stabilize and then remove/reserve lower. I'll annotate the incident. also filing a follow-up ticket to add an automated detector: "small payload, sudden concurrency spike -> enforce tenant batch cap or auto-reserve"

ingrid: filed ticket INF-4921: auto-burst-protect heuristics + alert rule. linking to logs and KV cache metrics.

mike: taking action items: - doc change for support runbook on temp reservation & batch-cap patch - add a console quick-button to 'isolate tenant for 1h' - follow up with customer on client-side retries

samira: customer asked for a permanent option: dedicated burst pool vs reserved capacity. I sent pricing and options.

mike: note for postmortem: root cause likely client-side session id rotation causing cache churn + sudden fanout -> batching window expansion -> queueing. mitigation combo: reservation + tenant-level batch cap + client fix.

samira: closing loop: customer will confirm after their frontend fix. they'll ping back if it recurs. thanks all. :raised_hands:

mike: leaving monitoring alert rule enabled for 24h. if p99 > 500ms for mantisbay-prod-43 during that time I'll escalate to eng-runtime.

ryan: marking incident as mitigated.

incident-bot: incident MIT-2026-1843 set to mitigated by ryan at 2026-09-15T09:57:00Z

samira: tagging this for knowledge base entry under support/kb/tenant-throttle-mitigation.
